violated_contract: A persisted queue cursor that the backing store rejects, or that compares outside the ordered field's domain, must never be rebuilt verbatim on every visit. processing_backlog_worker._page seeded start_after straight from the stored summary fields: a cursor whose id is empty makes the SDK build a document name with a trailing slash, so Firestore rejects the page with InvalidArgument on every visit and the worker's catch-all logged only the exception type — a per-owner stall (#23827, 78 paid owners with state=processing and 1-7 day old holds) that no log could type. A null at compares below every number, so the same page silently returns empty forever and can finish a choice whose audio is still held. The deferral must carry the failing call site and the stored cursor's shape, and the repair must be the same widening-preserving rewind finish() already uses for skipped scope.
canonical_prevention: Validate the stored cursor before seeding start_after: accept only finite non-bool numbers or datetimes for at and a non-empty slash-free string id; anything else logs event=processing_backlog outcome=cursor_invalid with the uid, kind, reason and value types, then rewinds to newest. The worker and sweep catch-alls log exc_info with the uid so the next deferral is typable from one log line. The guard matrix pins every rejected shape, a loopback-SDK test proves the rewound page is the cursorless wire shape and that a poisoned owner still drains and leaves valid cursors behind, and a loopback Firestore emulator proof reproduces the server's InvalidArgument for the empty-id cursor so the mechanism stays anchored to real behavior.
